Inherited haemorrhagic disorders Inherited disorders that lead to abnormal bleeding include platelet disorders and disturbances in clotting factors. Inherited platelet disorders can affect platelet function, size, and number. Platelet function disorders include ab- normalities in platelet receptors (such as Glanzmann’s thrombasthenia), platelet granules (storage pool deficien- cies), signal transduction pathways and granule release, and membrane phospholipids.1,2 Treatment depends on the disorder
